title: United Arab Emirates, Canada to share details of strategic partnership today
summary: Abu Dhabi's crown prince is in Ottawa for meetings today as Canada and the United Arab Emirates work to cement trade ties.

image.caption: Prime Minister Mark Carney hosts Sheikh Khaled bin Mohamed bin Zayed Al Nahyan, crown prince of Abu Dhabi, U.A.E., at a state dinner in Ottawa on Monday. (Adrian Wyld/The Canadian Press)

blocks.text: Abu Dhabi's crown prince is in Ottawa for meetings today as Canada and the United Arab Emirates work to cement trade ties.
U.A.E. has pledged to invest about $70 billion in Canada
Prime Minister Mark Carney will greet and participate in a welcome ceremony for Sheikh Khaled bin Mohamed bin Zayed Al Nahyan on Parliament Hill, before the pair take part in a signing ceremony.
Canada and the U.A.E. concluded negotiations on a free trade agreement earlier this year, in what both countries have called a "record" time of 47 days.
Carney hosted a state dinner for the crown prince in downtown Ottawa on Monday, where he said the countries are bound by a shared determination to "build for the future."
The prime minister said the leaders would share details of a strategic partnership today.
Carney visited the United Arab Emirates last November, when the U.A.E. pledged to invest around $70 billion in Canada.
